# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-saturation-medium

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

Runs `coop --git` (two agents with messaging and a shared git remote) on the 50-pair `flash` subset with the same setup as the `low` and `high` thinking runs (`gemini-3.8-flash`, 500 steps, compaction at 64K tokens, step counter, `$40` per-agent cost cap), changing only the thinking level to `medium`, Google's default for this model. It completes the `low` / `medium` / `high` comparison used to pick one thinking level for all later experiments. It ran as two 25-pair halves on two API keys and was merged into this one run.

## Observations

- 38/50 (76%), the highest score of any run on these 50 pairs so far, `solo` included. `coop --git` scored 30/50 at `low` (twice) and 34/50 at `high`; `solo` scored 36/50 and 32/50 at `low` and 34/50 at `high`.
- Pair by pair against `coop --git` at `low` (AI Studio run): 8 pairs passed only at `medium` and none only at `low` (exact two-sided test, p = 0.008). Against `high`: 4 only at `medium`, 0 only at `high`. Against `solo` at `low`: 3 only here, 1 only in `solo` (`pillow_task/290` (3,5)).
- It passed 2 pairs that no `solo` run has ever solved: `huggingface_datasets_task/3997` (2,4) and `samuelcolvin_dirty_equals_task/43` (3,7). The only pairs `solo` has solved that this run missed are `dspy_task/8394` (3,5) and `pillow_task/290` (3,5).
- Both `pallets_click_task/2068` pairs passed. At `low` and `high` thinking, agents there worked around a line of code both features needed, and the workaround failed hidden tests. Here one agent changed that line for both features: on (6,7) it passes both `process_priority` and `escape_shell` to the shared `Editor(...)` call.
- All 50 pairs merged without conflicts (44 clean, 6 identical branches), no agent reached the step limit, and pairs exchanged a median of 28 messages. Cost `$81.68` (`$1.63` per pair) vs. `$39.85` at `low` and `$96.17` at `high`.
